2609.18591.title: Recursive Reasoning or Statistical Extrapolation? In-Context Learning in Multi-Agent Interdependent Decision-Making
2609.18591.paper_summary: In-context learning (ICL) enables large language model (LLM) agents to improve decisions using interaction history, yet it remains unclear whether such improvement reflects refined internal reasoning or mere extrapolation of statistical patterns. To disentangle these mechanisms, we study LLM agents in multi-agent incomplete-information games that require recursive belief reasoning. By constructing a public goods game and manipulating the statistical structure of historical feedback, we evaluate decision quality against a history-independent rational expectations equilibrium (REE) benchmark. Our experiments reveal that when historical statistical patterns are disrupted, the benefits of longer context largely vanish, degrading decision quality to the no-context baseline in a way sharply amplified by stronger strategic interdependence. These results suggest that, in such strategic environments, ICL behavior is more consistent with statistical extrapolation than with strategic reasoning. Our work extends the mechanistic study of ICL to strategic multi-agent settings, introduces REE as a diagnostic tool for distinguishing reasoning from extrapolation, and provides a reusable framework for probing the boundaries of LLM reasoning in recursive belief tasks.
2609.18591.paper_summary_zh: 在情境學習（ICL）中，大型語言模型（LLM）代理能夠利用互動歷史來改善決策，但目前尚不清楚這種改善是否反映了精緻的內部推理或僅僅是統計模式的外推。為了釐清這些機制，我們研究了在需要遞歸信念推理的多代理不完全信息遊戲中的LLM代理。通過構建公共物品遊戲並操縱歷史反饋的統計結構，我們將決策質量與歷史無關的理性預期均衡（REE）基準進行評估。我們的實驗顯示，當歷史統計模式受到干擾時，較長的上下文所帶來的好處大部分消失，決策質量退化到無上下文基準，這種退化在更強的戰略相互依賴下被顯著放大。這些結果表明，在這種戰略環境中，ICL行為更符合統計外推而非戰略推理。我們的工作將ICL的機制研究擴展到戰略多代理設置，引入REE作為區分推理與外推的診斷工具，並提供一個可重用的框架，以探究LLM在遞歸信念任務中的推理邊界。
